name: Selleasy
summary: Shopify upsell and cross-sell app (by Logbase): bundles and product add-ons on the product page, add-on pop-ups and response-based funnels on the cart, one-click post-purchase offers and thank-you page add-ons. Flat plans with no order limit and no share of upsell revenue, including a free plan with up to five campaigns.
best_for: shopify stores that want bundles, add-ons, cart funnels and post-purchase offers out of one app on a flat fee that never takes a share of upsell revenue — small stores can test on the free plan, and Shopify Plus stores get checkout upsells from $29 a month
skip_if: you want more than 5 campaigns for free, or you already have an upsell app you like: Selleasy's strength is the low flat price, and its own pricing page still disagrees with itself about how it charges
honest_knock:
The pricing changed under this review in October 2026, and the vendor's own page has not caught up. The App Store listing now shows four flat plans with unlimited orders; logbase.io/selleasy/pricing shows the same plans in its cards and comparison table but still carries a block with the old order-based ladder and the line 'Priced on total store orders, not app orders'. Merchants who installed earlier may still be on the old ladder. Look at the charge Shopify shows at install rather than at either page.

The free plan now caps campaigns instead of orders: up to 5, against unlimited from Starter at $9. Five is enough for a test, not for a store that wants a separate offer on each collection.

Starter says '50 free AI recommendations' with no period attached, while Pro says '1,000 AI recommendations / month' and Max '2,500 AI recommendations / month'. The contrast suggests the 50 is a one-off allowance, but neither page says so outright. Ask before you plan around it.

And treat the vendor's headline claims as claims: the 20% AOV increase and the 40,000+ brands are Logbase's own figures on its own site, with no methodology attached to either.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter · per month, flat, unlimited orders and campaigns
pricing.notes:
(prices read 2026-10-30 on apps.shopify.com/upsell-cross-sell-kit-1 and on logbase.io/selleasy/pricing; the order-based ladder read on 19 September and 20 October 2026 has been replaced) Billed in USD through Shopify, recurring charges every 30 days. Four flat plans, each with unlimited orders. Free costs nothing and allows up to 5 campaigns, with the 18 upsell and cross-sell strategies, Shopify and manual recommendations, and chat, email and Zoom support. Starter is $9 a month or $91 a year and adds unlimited campaigns, 50 free AI recommendations and free setup on a call. Pro is $29 a month or $295 a year and adds 1,000 AI recommendations a month, an AI campaign optimizer, checkout upsells for Shopify Plus, advanced campaign targeting and metafield bulk recommendations. Max is $59 a month or $601 a year and adds 2,500 AI recommendations a month, advanced customizations, a rules engine, an AOV advisor and priority support. The paid plans carry a 30-day free trial. An Enterprise plan is quoted on request.

What changed: until October 2026 Starter was priced by your store's total monthly orders (free to 50, $9 to 500, $19 to 1,000, $29 above), and Pro and Max were $49 and $99. Logbase's pricing page still carries a block with that old ladder next to the new plan cards and comparison table on 30 October 2026; the App Store listing, which is what Shopify bills from, shows only the flat plans. Check the charge Shopify shows at install.

compare_with.name: UpsellPlus
compare_with.why:
Both cover the same surfaces — product page, cart, checkout, post-purchase — so the difference that matters is what you are billed for. UpsellPlus meters the upsell revenue the app is allowed to generate for you, and that meter does not stop where the pricing page appears to: $500 a month on free and on its $49 plan, $2,000 at $119, then a Scale ladder that runs $199 up to $5,000, $299 up to $10,000, $399 up to $15,000, $499 up to $20,000, $699 up to $30,000, $799 up to $40,000 and $999 with no ceiling. Only the $199 step is published; UpsellPlus support confirmed the rest in writing on 21 September 2026, and a store that passes $5,000 is moved to the $299 tier automatically, so the bill rises by itself.

Selleasy charges a flat plan instead and never touches the revenue: Free with up to 5 campaigns, $9 for unlimited campaigns, $29 for Pro with the AI layer and Plus checkout upsells, all with unlimited orders (App Store listing, read 30 October 2026). That makes the two apps diverge hardest exactly where an upsell app is working: at $20,000 of upsell revenue a month UpsellPlus is $499 and Selleasy is still $9 to $29. Run your own upsell revenue through UpsellPlus's ladder before you compare entry prices.

Check the Plus question on both. On UpsellPlus their FAQ says Shopify Plus is required only for checkout customization and checkout upsells, which is Shopify's restriction rather than theirs; cart, product page, drawer, thank-you and post-purchase offers work without it. On Selleasy the checkout upsells sit on Pro at $29 a month.
